phase3_findings.description: The helper's exit-code->token mapping (0->dismissed, 3->dismiss-refused, *->dismiss-failed) was never produced by a real run: the gh stub always exited 0 for the dismissals PUT, so dismiss-refused and dismiss-failed were untested branches in shipped code; a swapped 3)/*) arm would ship green.

The dismisser-missing partial-copy branch was masked by the deriver-missing check firing first; and the no-warning behavior on legitimate-refusal outcomes (no-dismiss-reject / no-dismiss-undetermined) was unasserted.

The devflow.yml step comment 'warn on the arms where a REJECT may still block' read as if it enumerated all such arms, when it names only the subset judged worth a maintainer alert (the undetermined arm also leaves a REJECT undismissed but is deliberately not warned).

The step if: gate matches /prflow:review only and not the transitional /devflow:review alias; fails toward no-dismissal and is byte-consistent with the sibling reach-record and stall-backstop steps (same population). Not changed: broadening only this step's alias handling would be an asymmetric change across a family of sibling steps, and it fails safe.

fix_decisions.claim_text: the /prflow:review-only gate does not cover the /devflow:review transitional alias
fix_decisions.evidence: byte-consistent with the sibling reach-record and stall-backstop steps; fails toward no dismissal; broadening only this step would be an asymmetric family change

parking_evidence.basis: the finding fails safe and matches the established sibling gate; broadening alias handling is a separate cross-step consistency change out of this issue's scope
parking_evidence.failing_input: a /devflow:review command reaching the command job — would skip the net, leaving Phase 4.4 as the path (fail-safe)
parking_evidence.source: .github/workflows/devflow.yml reach-record and stall-backstop steps use the same '/prflow:review ' gate
